summary: TaskOutput is partially aligned. Go now has a real background task manager, persisted runtime-task records, blocking waits, output files, and tests for basic shell/agent output. It still diverges from the TS baseline in the API/tool metadata contract, structured result payload, supported task/runtime types, local-agent output synthesis, notified/consumed lifecycle, wait cancellation and timeout semantics, output-file robustness, and parity test coverage.

gaps.title: Tool metadata, aliases, and input validation are not TS-equivalent
gaps.description: TS declares a strict object schema with semanticBoolean default block=true and timeout constrained to 0..600000 ms, marks the tool shouldDefer=true with maxResultSizeChars=100000, exposes aliases AgentOutputTool and BashOutputTool, and describes the tool as deprecated in favor of reading the output file. Go publishes only a loose JSONSchema without default/min/max/additionalProperties, manually defaults block but does not clamp timeout, returns a non-deprecated description, and TaskOutputTool does not implement AliasedTool even though the registry supports aliases.
gaps.impact: Model-facing availability, legacy tool names, invalid-input behavior, and timeout edge cases can differ from TS before the runtime path is even reached.

gaps.title: Go returns only rendered text instead of the TS structured TaskOutput payload
gaps.description: TS call() returns data shaped as {retrieval_status:'success'|'timeout'|'not_ready', task:null|TaskOutput}, then mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam renders the XML-like text. Go builds the XML-like text directly and returns StringResponse, so callers cannot observe or preserve the typed task object, prompt/result fields, or task:null timeout shape separately from rendered content.
gaps.impact: SDK/runtime consumers, UI renderers, deferred-tool plumbing, and parity fixtures that compare raw tool data cannot match TS behavior even when the visible text happens to look similar.

gaps.title: TaskOutput covers fewer task runtime types than TS
gaps.description: TS TaskOutput is wired against AppState.tasks and explicitly handles local_bash, local_agent, and remote_agent while the broader TaskState union includes additional background-capable task types. Go TaskOutput is tied to BackgroundTaskManager snapshots, whose concrete task types are only local_bash and local_agent. Go remote launches return a remote_launched Agent result with taskId/outputFile, but no remote_agent RuntimeTaskRecord is registered for TaskOutput Snapshot/Wait.
gaps.impact: Task IDs produced by Go remote-agent paths, and any future non-shell/non-local-agent background tasks, cannot be inspected through TaskOutput the way TS remote sessions can be.

gaps.title: Local-agent output synthesis can return noisy/raw output instead of TS clean final result
gaps.description: TS local_agent TaskOutput deliberately prefers the in-memory final assistant text (extractTextContent(agentTask.result.content)) over the disk transcript because the disk output may be a full JSONL transcript. Go TaskOutput reads snap.OutputPath first and falls back to snap.Result only when the file is blank. The existing Go test covers blank-file fallback, but not the noisy-file case where Result should override streamed/transcript output.
gaps.impact: For local agents that write progress, JSONL, or tool transcript content to the output file, Go can expose a different and less useful output than TS, and structured prompt/result fields are unavailable to UI-equivalent renderers.

gaps.title: Terminal output reads do not mark tasks as notified/consumed
gaps.description: TS marks a terminal task as notified when TaskOutput successfully retrieves it, and task-specific notification code atomically checks notified to avoid duplicate completion notices. Go RuntimeTaskRecord already has a Notified field, but BackgroundTask does not carry it, recordLocked does not persist it, TaskOutput never updates it, and completion hooks are emitted independently of TaskOutput consumption.
gaps.impact: Go cannot reproduce TS duplicate-notification suppression, consumed-state tracking, or terminal-task eviction semantics around TaskOutput reads.

gaps.title: Blocking wait semantics ignore context cancellation and mishandle timeout edge cases
gaps.description: TS waitForTaskCompletion checks toolUseContext.abortController every 100 ms and timeout=0 is a valid schema value that immediately returns the current task, causing running/pending tasks to render retrieval_status=timeout. Go TaskOutput discards the Execute context, passes only a duration into BackgroundTaskManager.Wait, and treats timeout<=0 as the omitted case by defaulting to 30 seconds before calling Wait.
gaps.impact: A cancelled Go tool call can keep blocking until timeout or task completion, timeout=0 is not an immediate non-wait check, and negative/oversized timeout values take paths TS schema validation would reject.

gaps.title: Output-file storage and read robustness differ from TS
gaps.description: TS task output paths live under a session-scoped project temp directory that is auto-readable and memoized across /clear, writes use O_NOFOLLOW where available, getTaskOutput tails up to 8 MB and returns empty output for read errors after logging, and formatTaskOutput then applies a 32k/160k character cap. Go stores output under project .claude/task-output, uses a 50 MB rotating writer opened without O_NOFOLLOW, reads only 64 KiB before formatting, and surfaces non-ENOENT read failures as tool errors. With TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH above 64 KiB, Go cannot return as much tail content as TS can.
gaps.impact: Large-output tails, symlink/security behavior, session isolation, auto-read assumptions, and transient read-error behavior can all differ from TS.

gaps.title: Parity tests do not cover the TS behavior matrix
gaps.description: Go tests cover basic shell success, non-blocking not_ready, blocking timeout, large-tail truncation, blank-file agent result fallback, and failed-agent output. They do not lock TS parity for aliases on the registry, strict/default/min/max schema semantics, timeout=0, context cancellation, remote_agent TaskOutput, notified state updates, typed payload preservation, or the local-agent noisy-output clean-result preference.
gaps.impact: Several high-risk runtime and output differences can regress or remain unnoticed because the current tests mostly assert visible substrings on a narrow local_bash/local_agent path.

candidate_tasks.title: Align TaskOutput tool metadata, aliases, and input validation
candidate_tasks.objective: Make Go TaskOutput expose the same model-facing metadata and input contract as TS, including legacy aliases and timeout/default validation behavior.
implementation_steps: Add Aliases() []string to TaskOutputTool returning AgentOutputTool and BashOutputTool.
Update Description() and any prompt/tool metadata surface to match the TS deprecated Read-output-file guidance.
Represent block default=true and timeout min=0/max=600000 in the Go validation path, even if JSONSchema cannot express all constraints yet.
Distinguish omitted timeout from explicit timeout=0 so explicit zero behaves like TS.
Add tests for aliases, omitted block, explicit false block, timeout=0, negative timeout, and timeout>600000.
acceptance_criteria: registry.Get("AgentOutputTool") and registry.Get("BashOutputTool") resolve to TaskOutput.
Omitting block waits by default, while block=false remains non-blocking.
timeout=0 is accepted and does not wait for a running task.
Negative and >600000 timeout inputs are rejected or surfaced exactly like the agreed TS schema-validation equivalent.
The public description communicates deprecation in favor of reading the task output file.
risks: The shared JSONSchema type may need a small extension for defaults/min/max/strictness; keep that change backward-compatible for other tools.
non_goals: Do not change Bash or Agent launch behavior except where tests need task IDs.

candidate_tasks.title: Add structured TaskOutput payload and render from it
candidate_tasks.objective: Preserve the TS TaskOutputToolOutput shape in Go while keeping the current XML-like text rendering for model-facing content.
implementation_steps: Define Go structs equivalent to TS TaskOutput and TaskOutputToolOutput.
Make Execute build the structured payload first for success, timeout, not_ready, and missing/null task cases.
Render Content from that payload using a small renderer equivalent to TS mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam.
Carry structured data through ToolResult using the repo's existing structured-content mechanism or a narrowly scoped payload field.
Add tests that assert both structured fields and rendered content.
acceptance_criteria: TaskOutput success exposes retrieval_status=success and a task object with task_id, task_type, status, description, output, optional exitCode/error/prompt/result.
Blocking timeout for an existing running task exposes retrieval_status=timeout and the current task object.
Timeout/missing paths can represent task:null where TS does.
Rendered Content remains compatible with the TS XML-like output format.
No unrelated tool loses existing text output behavior.
risks: Structured ToolResult propagation may touch shared loop/result-store code; keep payload support opt-in and test existing tools.
non_goals: Do not change the visible TaskOutput XML tags beyond TS parity.
Do not migrate all tools to structured output in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Broaden TaskOutput runtime coverage to remote-agent task IDs
candidate_tasks.objective: Ensure task IDs emitted by Go remote-agent launches can be queried by TaskOutput with a remote_agent snapshot equivalent to TS.
dependencies: taskoutput-gap-02 is recommended first if structured payload fields are required in the same patch.
implementation_steps: Add a remote_agent runtime record/snapshot type that stores task ID, status/phase, command/prompt, description, output path, and error/result where available.
When isolation=remote spawn succeeds, persist a remote_agent record before returning the launch result.
Wire polling/completion updates from RemoteRuntimeProvider into the runtime record or document the minimum TaskOutput status available before terminal completion.
Teach TaskOutput to render remote_agent snapshots with prompt/command and output content following TS.
Add a fake RemoteRuntimeProvider test that launches remote, queries TaskOutput, advances to terminal, and queries again.
acceptance_criteria: A taskId returned by Agent isolation=remote is accepted by TaskOutput.
TaskOutput returns task_type remote_agent for remote task IDs.
Running remote tasks return not_ready or timeout according to block/timeout settings.
Terminal remote tasks return success with status and output/error fields matching the persisted remote state.
Local_bash and local_agent TaskOutput behavior remains unchanged.
risks: Remote provider implementations may not always return outputFile or terminal output; tests should define the minimum compatible fallback behavior.
non_goals: Do not implement a real remote backend.
Do not add support for every TS task union member unless a separate audit scopes those task types.

candidate_tasks.title: Mirror TS local-agent clean-result output synthesis
candidate_tasks.objective: Make Go local_agent TaskOutput prefer the clean final agent result over raw output-file content when a final result is available, matching TS getTaskOutputData.
dependencies: taskoutput-gap-02 if prompt/result must be exposed as structured fields in the same delivery.
implementation_steps: Centralize TaskOutput output selection for local_agent snapshots.
If snap.Type is local_agent and snap.Result is non-empty, use snap.Result for output even when the output file has streamed content.
Keep output-file fallback for running agents and terminal agents with no clean result.
Expose prompt/result/error in the structured payload if structured TaskOutput support exists.
Add a test where an agent writes noisy/progress text to the output file but returns a clean final result.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal local_agent TaskOutput with Result set returns the clean result, not the noisy output file.
Blank-file result fallback continues to pass.
Running local_agent TaskOutput still returns available file output for progress checks.
Error fields remain visible for failed agents.
risks: Some Go callers may currently rely on TaskOutput showing streamed agent logs after completion; preserve logs through the output file path rather than the primary output field.
non_goals: Do not change SendMessage transcript restoration.
Do not rewrite agent session storage.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement TaskOutput notified/consumed lifecycle
candidate_tasks.objective: Use the existing RuntimeTaskRecord.Notified concept to mirror TS consumption semantics when TaskOutput reads terminal tasks.
implementation_steps: Add Notified to BackgroundTask and BackgroundTaskSnapshot or an equivalent consumed-state API on BackgroundTaskManager.
Persist Notified in recordLocked and snapshotFromRecord.
When TaskOutput returns success for a terminal task, atomically mark the task notified and save the record.
Ensure notification/hook emission checks the consumed state where TS would suppress redundant task notifications.
Add tests for block=false terminal success and block=true terminal success marking Notified, plus a duplicate-notification suppression case.
acceptance_criteria: RuntimeTaskRecord.Notified becomes true after TaskOutput successfully consumes a completed/failed/killed task.
Running/not_ready TaskOutput does not mark the task notified.
Terminal notification emission is not duplicated when TaskOutput already consumed the result.
Persisted records retain Notified across BackgroundTaskManager restart.
risks: Go hook notifications are less tightly coupled to model pending notifications than TS; define exactly which hook path should be suppressible before editing.
non_goals: Do not remove existing hook support.
Do not implement a full TS AppState eviction system in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Make TaskOutput wait and output reads context-aware and TS-robust
candidate_tasks.objective: Align blocking waits, cancellation, timeout=0, large-tail reads, output path safety, and read-error behavior with TS as closely as the Go runtime allows.
dependencies: taskoutput-gap-01 should land first for timeout validation/default distinction if possible.
implementation_steps: Thread context.Context through TaskOutput Execute into BackgroundTaskManager.Wait.
Make Wait stop promptly on context cancellation while preserving timeout status for ordinary deadlines.
Preserve explicit timeout=0 as an immediate wait attempt rather than defaulting to 30 seconds.
Increase the pre-format tail read limit to match TS's 8 MB or compute it from TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH so larger configured max lengths are honored.
Consider O_NOFOLLOW or equivalent safeguards for output file opens on supported platforms.

Match TS read-error semantics for task output files: ENOENT returns empty output; other read errors should be logged/represented according to an explicit parity decision instead of surprising infrastructure failure.
acceptance_criteria: A cancelled TaskOutput context returns promptly without waiting for the full timeout.
timeout=0 on a running task returns immediately with the TS-equivalent timeout/not_ready behavior chosen by the validation task.
TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=160000 can return more than 64 KiB of tail content when the file contains enough data.
Missing output files produce an empty output field, not a tool failure.
Existing success/not_ready/timeout tests still pass.
risks: Changing output-file paths or O_NOFOLLOW behavior may require platform-specific test handling on Windows.
non_goals: Do not redesign background task storage layout unless required for security parity.
Do not change Bash foreground output truncation.

candidate_tasks.title: Add a TaskOutput parity test matrix
candidate_tasks.objective: Lock the TS TaskOutput behavior matrix with focused Go tests so future implementation work has clear red/green targets.
implementation_steps: Add alias and schema/default tests for TaskOutput.
Add timeout=0 and context-cancel tests.
Add structured payload tests if the payload task has landed, otherwise add TODO-marked red tests under a parity/alignment naming convention.
Add local_agent clean-result-over-noisy-file tests.
Add Notified state tests against RuntimeTaskStore.
Add remote_agent TaskOutput tests with a fake RemoteRuntimeProvider.
acceptance_criteria: The test matrix explicitly covers success, not_ready, timeout, missing task, failed task, terminal notified consumption, local_agent clean result, remote_agent lookup, alias resolution, and timeout validation.
Tests assert semantic fields rather than only broad substrings where structured data is available.
Tests can be run independently with a narrow go test -run expression.
risks: Some tests may intentionally fail until implementation tasks land; mark them clearly if this repo allows red alignment tests.
non_goals: Do not rewrite unrelated task-tool tests.
Do not add external services or network calls to cover remote-agent behavior.
